title: Hyundai Declares Physical AI Strategy at SF AI Summit
summary: Executive Chair Euisun Chung used the San Francisco AI Summit to reposition Hyundai Motor Group as a physical AI company spanning autonomous driving, robotics and 'AI Defined Factories'. The plan leans on Boston Dynamics for robotics and on a data flywheel that feeds real-world operational data back into model training. Chung announced a Robot Reference Platform co-developed with NVIDIA, a new Advanced Vehicle Platform unit in Silicon Valley led by Jeremy Ma, and domestic investments including the roughly $6.2 billion Saemangeum AI Valley.
whyItMatters: The interesting claim is the data flywheel, not the capital: Hyundai is arguing that owning factories and vehicle fleets is the scarce asset in physical AI, because that is where operational data comes from. If that holds, incumbent manufacturers — not model labs — end up with the training-data moat for embodied intelligence.
